children: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) shares gained more than 1 percent in early trade on Monday after Citi and Goldman Sachs retained their 'Buy' calls on the defence PSU, citing improving execution across fighter aircraft, trainers and helicopters as supply constraints ease and deliveries gather pace.

Citi maintained its 'Buy' rating on HAL with a target price of Rs 6,175 per share, implying an upside of nearly 29 percent from Friday's closing price of Rs 4,800.30. Goldman Sachs also retained its 'Buy' call with a target of Rs 5,870, indicating potential upside of about 22 percent.

HAL shares rose 1.33 percent to Rs 4,864 in early trade on Monday. The stock had gained 0.26 percent on Friday and is up 9.2 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen 10.7 percent over the same period. HAL's market capitalisation stood at about Rs 3.21 lakh crore.
At 9:17 am, the Sensex was up 337 points, or 0.45 percent, at 74,631.98, while the Nifty was up 19 points, or 0.08 percent, at 23,365.25.

Citi sees execution improving across HAL platforms

Citi said HAL's recent handovers demonstrated improving execution across multiple platforms. The company handed over the final two LCA Tejas FOC twin-seat trainers and three HTT-40 basic trainers to the Indian Air Force, as well as four Dhruv Next Generation helicopters to Pawan Hans on September 18.
The brokerage said execution of the Dhruv NG programme was progressing well and remained on schedule. HAL management is targeting delivery of 10 LCA Mk-1A aircraft by March 2027.

HAL has so far received 10 F404 engines, with further deliveries expected. Citi expects improving engine availability and progress on aircraft testing to reduce the remaining execution overhang surrounding the Mk-1A programme.

The start of Mk-1A deliveries has been a key monitorable for HAL. Citi had earlier said that commencement of deliveries could ease the execution overhang and shift investor attention towards the company's multi-year growth visibility and large order backlog.
Goldman Sachs: Focus shifting to converting backlog into revenue

Goldman Sachs similarly said HAL's latest deliveries pointed to improving execution across fighter, trainer and helicopter platforms. The brokerage maintained its 'Buy' recommendation and Rs 5,870 target price.

The brokerage noted that GE has delivered another three F404 engines, supporting production of the LCA Mk-1A. As supply constraints ease and aircraft move through production and testing, Goldman Sachs expects the focus to increasingly shift towards HAL's ability to convert its large order backlog into revenue.
The brokerage said the improvement in deliveries was also aligned with the government's push towards indigenous aerospace and defence manufacturing.

HAL's latest handovers included the final two twin-seat trainers under the original 40-aircraft LCA Mk-1 order. The company will now increasingly turn its attention to the much larger Mk-1A programme, covering 180 aircraft ordered by the Indian Air Force.

The stock's near-term outlook, therefore, remains closely tied to the pace at which improving F404 engine supplies and completion of testing translate into actual LCA Mk-1A deliveries, while the recent HTT-40 and Dhruv NG handovers provide evidence of improving execution beyond the Tejas programme.
